items.title: Overdraft fee on a debit card purchase or ATM withdrawal you never opted into
items.summary: Your bank cannot charge an overdraft fee for paying an ATM withdrawal or a one-time debit card purchase unless you opted in to its overdraft service and it sent you a confirmation. If you never opted in, the fee is not allowed. You can revoke an opt-in at any time.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You have a consumer bank or credit union account, and you were charged an overdraft fee, including a daily, sustained or negative-balance fee, for an ATM withdrawal or a one-time debit card purchase, and you never opted in.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.17(b)(1): the bank may not charge the fee unless it gave you a separate written notice of its overdraft service, got your affirmative opt-in, and sent you a written or electronic confirmation that states your right to revoke. Fees are allowed only for overdrafts paid on or after the date the bank received your opt-in (comment 17(c)-1). The ban also covers daily or sustained overdraft fees when the negative balance comes only from ATM or one-time debit card transactions (comment 17(b)-9). The bank cannot make you opt in to get checks or ACH payments covered, and must give you the same account terms if you do not opt in (12 CFR 1005.17(b)(2) and (b)(3)).

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Find the fee on your statement and note its date, its amount and the ATM or debit card transaction that caused it. 2. Contact your bank. Say you never opted in and ask it to refund the fee. If the bank says you opted in, ask for a copy of the confirmation it was required to send you. 3. If you opted in before and no longer want it, revoke it the same way you opted in. The bank must act on this as soon as reasonably practicable. 4. If the bank refuses, submit a complaint to the CFPB online or by phone at (855) 411-2372.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: On [date] you charged me an overdraft fee of [amount] for an ATM withdrawal or one-time debit card purchase. I never opted in to your overdraft service for these transactions, so under 12 CFR 1005.17 this fee is not allowed. Please refund [amount], or send me a copy of the written confirmation of my opt-in.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: The rule covers only ATM and one-time debit card transactions. Checks, ACH payments and recurring debit card payments can still bring overdraft fees without an opt-in. It does not apply when the overdraft is paid from an overdraft line of credit, a credit card or a transfer from your savings account. If a debit card purchase was approved while you had enough money but your balance was short when it settled, the bank still cannot charge you an overdraft fee unless you opted in (comment 17(b)-1.iv).

actions.label: CFPB: overdraft fees you did not opt into

items.title: Unauthorized or wrong debit card charge or electronic transfer
items.summary: If you report an unauthorized or incorrect electronic transfer within 60 days after your bank sent the statement that first shows it, the bank must investigate. It has 10 business days, or up to 45 days if it puts the money back into your account provisionally within 10 business days. If there was an error, the bank must fix it within one business day, including interest and refunds of the fees it charged because of the error.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You have a consumer bank, credit union or other account covered by Regulation E, and you see an unauthorized transfer, a wrong amount, a missing transfer, a math error by the bank, or the wrong amount of cash from an ATM. Your loss for unauthorized use is capped at $50 if you report a lost or stolen card within two business days after you learn of it, and generally at $500 if you report later.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.11 (error resolution) and 12 CFR 1005.6 (limits on your liability). The bank must receive your notice no later than 60 days after it sent the statement that first shows the error (12 CFR 1005.11(b)(1)(i)). It must decide within 10 business days, or within 45 days if it provisionally credits the amount, with interest where applicable, within 10 business days and tells you within two business days after crediting. It may hold back up to $50 for a suspected unauthorized transfer (12 CFR 1005.11(c)(2)(i)). It must fix an error within one business day after finding it and report results within three business days.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Contact your bank right away, in person, by phone or in writing. Give your name, your account number, why you think there is an error, and the type, date and amount. 2. If the bank asks you to confirm in writing, send it within 10 business days of your call. Otherwise the bank does not have to give you a provisional credit. 3. If your card was lost or stolen, report it within two business days after you learn of it. 4. Keep copies and note every call. 5. Watch for a provisional credit within 10 business days. 6. If the bank says there was no error, it must explain in writing, and you can ask for the documents it relied on. 7. If the bank does not follow the rules, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I am reporting an error on account [account number]. On [date] there was an electronic transfer of [amount] that I did not authorize. Under Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.11, please investigate, credit my account, and refund any fees and interest caused by this error.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Deadlines are longer in some cases: 20 business days instead of 10 for transfers within 30 days after the first deposit to a new account, and 90 days instead of 45 for point-of-sale debit card purchases, transfers not started in a U.S. state, and new accounts. The bank cannot charge you for the error-resolution process. It does not have to refund fees you would have paid anyway. If it takes back a provisional credit, it must tell you the date and amount and pay your checks and preauthorized transfers for five business days without overdraft charges. If you report an unauthorized transfer on a statement more than 60 days after the statement was sent, you can be liable for transfers after that 60-day period. Extenuating circumstances, such as long travel or a hospital stay, can extend the deadlines. If you let someone use your card, their charges count as authorized until you tell the bank they no longer have permission.

actions.label: CFPB: getting money back after an unauthorized transaction

items.title: Chase: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: Chase charges a $34 Overdraft Fee per transaction, up to 3 fees a business day ($102). There is no fee if your account ends the business day overdrawn by $50 or less. If you end the day more than $50 overdrawn, you have until 11 p.m. ET (8 p.m. PT) the next business day to deposit or transfer enough to get back to overdrawn by $50 or less.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $34 per transaction, charged in nightly processing, starting with the first transaction that takes you more than $50 below zero. Cap: 3 fees per business day, up to $102. Cushion: no fee if the account ends the business day overdrawn by $50 or less. Window: if the account ends a business day more than $50 overdrawn, you have until 11 p.m. ET (8 p.m. PT) the next business day to deposit or transfer enough that the account ends that day overdrawn by $50 or less. This is Chase Overdraft Assist. It is automatic and needs no enrollment.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Before 11 p.m. ET on the next business day, add money that counts the same day: cash, a check or a transfer from another Chase account at a Chase branch before it closes or at a Chase ATM, or a Chase-to-Chase transfer, Zelle or Chase QuickDeposit on chase.com or the app. Add enough to cover the overdraft plus anything else that may post that day, so the account ends the day no more than $50 below zero. You do not need to reach $0. Transfers from other banks may not arrive in time, and a check counts only if Chase places no hold on it. If a $34 fee still posts after you met the deadline, call Chase customer service or use chat, give the deposit date and amount, and ask for a review under Overdraft Assist.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: On [date] I deposited [amount] before 11 p.m. ET, and my account ended that business day overdrawn by $50 or less. Under Chase Overdraft Assist that means no Overdraft Fee, so please review and refund the fee that posted.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Overdraft Assist does not apply to Chase First Checking, Chase High School Checking or Chase Secure Checking. Business accounts have separate rules. If you miss the deadline, the fee is charged on the previous business day's transactions that overdrew the account. Chase charges no fee when it returns a transaction unpaid. You are responsible for the deadline even if no alert reaches you.

items.title: Citizens: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: Citizens charges a $35 Overdraft Fee per item, up to 5 a business day ($175), and no fee on an item of $5 or less or when the day ends $5 or less overdrawn. With Citizens Peace of Mind, if you deposit enough to bring your account to a positive available balance (not counting the fees) by 10 p.m. ET the following business day, the overdraft fees are reversed.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $35 per item paid. Cap: 5 fees per business day, up to $175. Cushion ($5 Overdraft Pass): no fee on an overdraft item of $5 or less, or when the account ends the business day overdrawn by $5 or less. Citizens Fee Relief: no Overdraft Fee on your first overdraft occurrence each year. Window (Citizens Peace of Mind): the fees are reversed if you deposit enough to bring the account to a positive available balance, not counting the overdraft fees, by 10 p.m. the following business day.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: By 10 p.m. ET the following business day, deposit money that is available that night: cash with a teller or at a Citizens ATM (ATM by 10 p.m. ET), a Citizens check with a teller or at a Citizens ATM (ATM by 10 p.m. ET), or an electronic direct deposit. Checks from other banks, including federal government checks, are available only the next business day, so they do not help in time. Bring the balance above $0, not just to $0; the fees themselves do not need to be covered. If the fees are not reversed, contact Citizens customer service and ask for a review under Peace of Mind.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My account was overdrawn on [date], and I deposited [amount] before 10 p.m. ET the following business day, which brought my available balance above zero not counting the fees. Under Citizens Peace of Mind those overdraft fees should be reversed, so please review and reverse them.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: These terms come from the Quest Checking and One Deposit Checking account guides on citizensbank.com (revised July 2025). The Peace of Mind line in the guide says 10:00 PM without a time zone; the same guide gives its deposit cutoffs in Eastern time. ATM and debit card overdrafts are paid only if you enroll in Debit Card Overdraft Coverage; otherwise they are declined at no cost. Paying an overdraft is at the bank's discretion. Other Citizens accounts may have different terms, so check your own account guide.

items.title: Huntington: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: On Huntington Perks Checking, the Overdraft Fee is $15 per item, up to 3 a day, and there is no fee unless the account ends the day overdrawn by more than $50. With 24-Hour Grace, the fees are generally waived if, by midnight CT of the next business day, you deposit enough to cover the overdrafts and that day's other transactions and the account is no more than $50 overdrawn.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $15 per overdraft item on Perks Checking. Cap: 3 fees per day. Cushion ($50 Safety Zone): no fee unless the final balance for the day is overdrawn by more than $50. Window (24-Hour Grace): on a business day that ends overdrawn with Overdraft Fees, the fees are generally waived if, before midnight CT at the end of the next business day, you deposit enough to cover all of the overdrafts plus any other transactions that post, and the account is not overdrawn by more than $50.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Make the deposit before midnight CT at the end of the next business day. Cover the prior day's overdrafts plus everything else that posts that day, because Huntington processes the current day's activity first. A deposit that covers only part may not get the fees waived. Log in to online banking or call Huntington to see which items count. If the fee still posts after you met the deadline, contact Huntington and ask for a review under 24-Hour Grace.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My account was overdrawn on [date], and I deposited [amount] before midnight CT the next business day to cover the overdrafts and that day's transactions. Under 24-Hour Grace those Overdraft Fees should be waived, so please review and reverse them.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: The fee depends on the account: the Perks Checking charges form lists $15, and the SmartInvest Checking form lists no Overdraft Fee. Huntington charges no Return Fee. ATM and debit card overdrafts are authorized only if you opt in. Huntington may remove 24-Hour Grace for unusual circumstances such as fraud. These terms come from Huntington's account charges forms (October 2026).

items.title: PNC: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: PNC charges at most one $36 overdraft item fee per day. With Extra Time on a Virtual Wallet Spend account, if the account goes negative on a business day, you have until 10 p.m. ET the next business day to bring your available balance to at least $0 and avoid the fee.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $36 overdraft item fee, at most one per day. No non-sufficient funds fee. Window (Extra Time, part of Low Cash Mode): the clock starts as soon as your available balance goes negative. You get at least 24 hours: until 10 p.m. ET on the next business day to bring your available balance to at least $0. A transaction on a Friday after 10 p.m. ET counts as Monday activity, so Extra Time ends Tuesday at 10 p.m. ET. If you miss it, a fee may apply for each business day that ends negative and on which you made or authorized new withdrawals that added to the negative balance.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Open the PNC Mobile App, where the Extra Time clock shows the time left. Deposit or transfer enough to reach at least $0 in available balance before 10 p.m. ET the next business day. Some deposit types, or deposits made late, may not be available before Extra Time ends, so use money that is available right away. In the app, go to Profile and Settings, then Low Cash Mode, to set alerts for when Extra Time begins and ends. If a $36 fee still posts after you reached $0 in time, contact PNC customer service and ask for a review.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My Virtual Wallet Spend account went negative on [date], and I deposited [amount] to bring the available balance to at least $0 before 10 p.m. ET the next business day. Under Extra Time no overdraft item fee should apply, so please review and refund the fee.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Low Cash Mode and Extra Time work only on the Spend account of a Virtual Wallet product, and Low Cash Mode is only in the PNC Mobile App. PNC pays overdrafts at its discretion. Payment Control, which lets you choose which checks and ACH items to pay or return, does not cover debit card transactions. The pages do not say whether Extra Time applies before you set up Low Cash Mode in the app.

items.title: Regions: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: Regions charges a $36 Paid Overdraft Item fee, up to 3 a day, and no fee when your personal checking account is overdrawn by $5 or less after nightly processing. If one business day's transactions take you more than $5 below zero, you have until 8 p.m. CT the next business day to add funds so the balance is positive or no more than $5 overdrawn.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $36 per paid overdraft item. Cap: 3 paid overdraft item fees per day. Cushion: no fee when the available balance is overdrawn by $5 or less after end-of-day processing. Window (Overdraft Grace): if one business day's transactions overdraw the available balance by more than $5, add funds by 8 p.m. CT the next business day so the balance after that night's processing is positive or no more than $5 overdrawn. If the day of your overdraft notice is a Saturday, Sunday or bank holiday, the deadline is 8 p.m. CT the next business day after the overdraft. No enrollment is needed.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Deposit cash at a Regions branch or ATM, or transfer from another Regions account in online banking, before 8 p.m. CT. Zelle, Cash App and Venmo deposits count only if they reach your available balance by 8 p.m. CT, and check deposits may be held. Cover the overdraft plus any new items and fees that post that day. Some deposit locations have cutoffs earlier than 8 p.m. CT. If the fee posts anyway, call Regions at 1-800-947-BANK (2265) and ask for a review.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: One business day's transactions overdrew my account on [date], and I deposited [amount] before 8 p.m. CT the next business day so my balance was no more than $5 overdrawn after nightly processing. Under Regions Overdraft Grace those Paid Overdraft Item fees should be waived, so please review and refund them.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Covers Regions consumer and Private Wealth Management personal checking accounts, except Now Checking and SafeGuard Checking. Money market accounts are not eligible. An Overdraft Grace deposit does not stop an NSF Review item from being returned unpaid. The 3-a-day cap comes from a Regions overdraft notice dated June 2023. The main page says Central Time; a Regions help page says Central Standard Time.

items.title: TD Bank: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: TD Bank charges $35 per overdraft, up to 3 fees per day per account, and no fee when you are overdrawn by $50 or less. If you end the business day more than $50 overdrawn, bring your available balance to at least $0 by 11 p.m. ET the next business day and the fee is refunded.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $35 per transaction that overdraws your available balance by more than $50. Cap: 3 fees per day per account. Cushion: no fee when you are overdrawn by $50 or less. Window (Grace Period): if you are more than $50 overdrawn at the end of the business day, you have until 11 p.m. ET the next business day to bring your available balance to at least $0, counting pending and posted items. The fee appears the next morning and is refunded right away. If the overdraft starts on a Saturday, Sunday or Monday, the deadline is Tuesday at 11 p.m. ET; a Friday start means Monday at 11 p.m. ET. If the deadline falls on a federal holiday, you have until 11 p.m. ET the following business day.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Use a method that posts before its cutoff: a transfer from another TD account online or by phone (11 p.m. ET), Zelle (11 p.m. ET), a wire from another bank (8 p.m. ET), cash or a TD transfer at a TD ATM (8 p.m. ET), or cash at a TD store before it closes. Only $100 of a check deposit is available the same day. Cover the overdraft plus any scheduled payments or checks that may post. The refund shows the morning after the deadline, and your statement lists your year-to-date Grace Period refunds. If the fee is not refunded, call 1-888-751-9000 and ask for a review.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My checking account went more than $50 negative on [date], and I deposited [amount] so my available balance was at least $0 before 11 p.m. ET the next business day. Under the TD Grace Period the overdraft fee should be refunded, so please review and credit it.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: The Grace Period and the $50 threshold apply only to personal and small business checking, not savings. TD Essential Banking has no overdraft services and no overdraft fees. There is no limit on the number of Grace Period refunds. A pending debit card transaction does not start a Grace Period until it posts. New transactions during the Grace Period can make you miss the refund.

items.title: U.S. Bank: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: U.S. Bank charges a $36 Overdraft Paid Fee per item, up to 3 a day. There is no fee if your available balance ends the business day overdrawn by $50 or less. If a fee is charged, a qualifying deposit that brings your available balance to $0 or more (not counting the fee) by 11 p.m. ET on the business day the fee was charged gets the fee waived automatically.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $36 Overdraft Paid Fee per item; no fee on items of $5 or less. Cap: 3 fees per day. Cushion: no fee if your available balance at the end of the business day is overdrawn by $50 or less. Window (Overdraft Fee Forgiven): the fee is charged on the business day after the overdraft, and you have until 11 p.m. ET that same day to bring your available balance to $0 or more. The deposit does not need to cover the fee. The bank's example: overdrawn by $90 on Wednesday, fee charged Thursday, a deposit of $90 or more by 11 p.m. ET Thursday and the fee is waived. Weekend transactions count as Monday's, so the fee posts Tuesday and the deadline is 11 p.m. ET Tuesday.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: As soon as you see the fee or the Overdraft Fee Forgiven alert, deposit enough to cover the negative balance by 11 p.m. ET that day. Use a qualifying deposit: cash, a check deposited in a branch, a U.S. Bank ATM deposit (before 8 p.m. local time for same-day credit), an ACH or other electronic deposit, a wire, or a transfer from another U.S. Bank account. Mobile check deposits generally do not count. Watch for new transactions until 11 p.m. ET. The waiver shows before the start of business the next morning as "Overdraft Paid Fee Waived – Forgiven." If it does not, call 24-Hour Banking at 800-USBANKS (872-2657) and ask for a review.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: An Overdraft Paid Fee was charged on [date], and before 11 p.m. ET that day I made a qualifying deposit of [amount] that brought my available balance to $0 or more. Under Overdraft Fee Forgiven the fee should be waived, so please review the account and reverse it.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Consumer checking accounts qualify except Safe Debit accounts; the page leads with Bank Smartly Checking. Deposits with an extended hold and deposits into accounts open less than 30 days generally do not qualify. The program does not reverse Overdraft Protection transfers or their fees. The fee still shows in your available balance until the 11 p.m. ET review. A U.S. Bank help article says the deposit must be made by 11 p.m. ET on the same day the balance went negative, so deposit that same day if you can.

items.title: Wells Fargo: overdraft fee grace period
items.summary: Wells Fargo charges $35 per overdraft item, up to 3 fees per business day on personal accounts. With Extra Day Grace Period, if your available balance is zero or positive by 11:59 p.m. ET on the next business day, the pending overdraft fees are waived. There is no fee on items of $10 or less.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fee: $35 per item paid into overdraft. Cap: 3 fees per business day on consumer accounts. Cushion: no fee on items of $10 or less, and no fee when both your ending daily balance and your available balance are overdrawn by $10 or less after all transactions post. Window: fees from an overdraft stay pending for one extra business day. If your available balance is zero or positive at 11:59 p.m. ET on that extra day, they are waived. If your balance covers only some items, it is applied in posting order and the items left uncovered are charged.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: On the business day after the overdraft, deposit or transfer enough to bring your available balance to zero or more before 11:59 p.m. ET, and count any other payments due that day. Use money that is available the same day, because deposits follow the bank's funds availability policy. If you have Overdraft Protection, the linked transfer runs first and the grace period then covers only items that still have a pending fee. If a $35 fee still posts after you met the deadline, call 1-800-TO-WELLS (1-800-869-3557) or visit a branch and ask for a review.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My account was overdrawn on [date], and I deposited [amount] so my available balance was zero or positive before 11:59 p.m. ET on the next business day. Under the Extra Day Grace Period those overdraft fees should be waived, so please review and refund the fee that posted.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: This page covers personal accounts. Clear Access Banking has no overdraft services and no overdraft fees. Business accounts pay $35 per item, up to 4 fees per business day. The bank pays overdrafts at its discretion. The page lists no enrollment step for the grace period. The page says 11:59 p.m. ET in most places but midnight ET in one FAQ, and one footnote says the balance must be positive rather than zero or positive, so aim to be above $0 before 11:59 p.m. ET.

items.title: Canceling or fixing a money transfer you sent abroad
items.summary: After you pay for an international money transfer, you have 30 minutes to cancel it, as long as the money has not been picked up or deposited. The provider must then refund everything you paid, including fees, within three business days. If something goes wrong, such as the money not arriving by the date on your receipt, you have 180 days from that date to report it, and the provider has 90 days to investigate.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You are a consumer in a U.S. state sending more than $15 electronically, for personal, family or household purposes, to a person at a location in another country, through a bank, credit union or money transfer company that sends remittances in the normal course of its business. A provider that sent 500 or fewer transfers in the previous year and sends 500 or fewer in the current year is not covered.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Regulation E, Subpart B. Cancellation: 12 CFR 1005.34. The request must be received no later than 30 minutes after you pay, and the refund of all funds, including fees and, to the extent not prohibited by law, taxes, is due within three business days. Transfers scheduled at least three business days ahead can be canceled up to three business days before the transfer date (12 CFR 1005.36(c)). Errors: 12 CFR 1005.33. Your notice must be received within 180 days after the disclosed date of availability. The provider has 90 days to investigate and three business days after that to report.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: To cancel: contact the provider within 30 minutes of paying. Give your name and your address or phone number, and identify the transfer. To report an error: contact the provider within 180 days after the date of availability printed on your receipt. Give your name and phone number or address, the recipient's name, the transfer, and why you think there is an error. If the provider finds an error, you choose the remedy, such as a refund or having the money made available to the recipient at no extra cost. If the money was not available by the promised date, the provider must also refund its fees. If the provider does not follow the rules, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I sent a transfer of [amount] on [date], confirmation number [number], to [recipient]. The money was not available by the date on my receipt. Under 12 CFR 1005.33, please investigate and [refund the transfer amount and all fees / make the money available to the recipient at no extra cost].

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: You cannot cancel once the money has been picked up or deposited. A late delivery is not an error if it was caused by extraordinary circumstances outside the provider's control, required fraud or legal screening, fraud by the sender, or a wrong account number you gave (when the provider meets certain conditions). If the delay was caused by wrong information you gave, the provider may keep fees charged by others, but not its own fee. The provider cannot charge you for the error investigation if an error occurred. A simple status question, or a change requested by the recipient, is not an error.

actions.label: CFPB: your rights on money transfers abroad

items.title: Wrong or unauthorized charge on your credit card bill
items.summary: If your written dispute reaches the card issuer within 60 days after it sent the first statement with the error, the issuer must acknowledge it within 30 days and resolve it within two complete billing cycles, and no later than 90 days. Until then you do not have to pay the disputed amount or the finance or other charges tied to it. If the error happened as you said, the issuer must credit the disputed amount and those related charges.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You have a credit card or other open-end credit account, and your statement shows a charge you did not make, a charge for goods or services you did not accept or that were not delivered as agreed, a payment or credit that was not posted, a math error, or a charge you want explained. A statement not sent to an address you gave in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle also counts.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Fair Credit Billing Act, Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.13. The notice must be written and received at the billing-error address no later than 60 days after the first statement showing the error (12 CFR 1026.13(b)). The issuer must acknowledge in writing within 30 days and resolve within 2 complete billing cycles, but no later than 90 days (12 CFR 1026.13(c)). While the dispute is open, the issuer may not try to collect the disputed amount or report it as delinquent (12 CFR 1026.13(d)).

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Call the issuer to report the problem right away if you want, but also send a letter. A call alone does not protect your rights. 2. Mail the letter to the address for billing inquiries, not the payment address, so it arrives within 60 days after the first statement with the error was sent. 3. Include your name, address, account number, and the type, date and amount of the error and why you think it is wrong. Attach copies of receipts, not originals. 4. Pay the part of the bill you do not dispute. 5. If you are on autopay, your notice must arrive at least 3 business days before the payment date to stop the disputed amount from being deducted. 6. Keep copies and dates. If the issuer does not follow the rules, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I am writing to dispute a billing error on account [account number]. My statement dated [date] shows a charge of [amount] that [I did not make / was for goods I did not receive]. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act and 12 CFR 1026.13, please correct the error and credit the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: The issuer can still collect the part of the bill you do not dispute, and it can lower your available credit by the disputed amount while it investigates. If it decides you owe the money, it must explain why in writing, send you copies of documents if you ask, and tell you when payment is due. You can still dispute a charge you already paid, but you may not get the money back until the issuer decides you were right. Your liability for unauthorized use of a credit card is capped at $50 (12 CFR 1026.12(b)). Errors on debit card or bank transfers follow Regulation E instead.

items.title: Refund of a credit balance on your credit card
items.summary: If your credit card or other open-end credit account has a credit balance of more than $1, the creditor must refund it within seven business days after it receives your written request. If a credit balance stays on the account for more than six months, the creditor must make a good-faith effort to refund it to you without a request.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You have a credit balance of more than $1 on a credit card or other open-end credit account. It can come from paying more than you owed, a merchant refund, or a rebate of unearned finance charges or insurance premiums.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.11(a): the creditor must credit the amount to your account, refund any part of the remaining credit balance within seven business days from receipt of your written request, and make a good-faith effort to refund any credit balance left on the account for more than six months.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Check your statement for the credit balance amount. 2. Send a written request to the card issuer. Say how you want the money paid: cash, check, money order, or a credit to your bank account. 3. Note the date the issuer received it. The refund is due within seven business days. 4. If you do nothing, the balance is applied to new purchases, and after six months the issuer must try to refund it. 5. If the issuer does not refund it, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: As of [date], my account [account number] has a credit balance of [amount]. Under 12 CFR 1026.11(a), please refund the full credit balance to me by [check / deposit to my bank account] within seven business days of receiving this request.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: The request must be in writing to start the seven-business-day clock. The issuer may also refund the balance without being asked. The six-month refund is not required if the issuer cannot find you through your last known address or phone number.

actions.label: OCC: refund of a credit balance

items.title: Refund of unused GAP and other add-ons when your car loan ends early
items.summary: When an auto loan ends early through payoff, refinancing, repossession or a total loss, you may be due a pro rata refund of the unused part of GAP and other add-on products paid up front. For an early payoff, the CFPB says the full refund should go to you. After a default, the refund should first reduce any amount you still owe. Your contract and state law set the exact terms.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You financed GAP, a vehicle service contract (extended warranty) or another add-on product as part of your auto loan, and the loan ended before its term because you paid it off, sold or refinanced the car, or the car was repossessed or declared a total loss.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: No single federal regulation sets the refund amount. It comes from your add-on contract and state law. The CFPB's consumer page says you may be entitled to a refund if you sell, refinance or prepay your auto loan. In its Supervisory Highlights, Issue 35 (Fall 2024), the CFPB found that servicers engaged in unfair acts or practices by failing to ensure refunds of unearned premiums after early termination, and by miscalculating or delaying refunds.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Find your financing contract and each add-on contract, and read the cancellation and refund terms. If you do not have them, ask your lender, the product provider or the dealer. 2. Ask in writing to cancel the product and to receive the refund of the unused portion. 3. Ask how the refund was calculated and where it was sent. After a repossession, ask to see the refund applied to your remaining balance. 4. If you get no refund or a wrong amount, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My auto loan [account number] ended on [date] because [I paid it off / the car was totaled / the car was repossessed]. Please cancel the GAP and other add-on products financed in this loan and refund the unused portion, [amount] if known. Please tell me in writing how you calculated the refund.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: GAP stops providing any benefit once the loan ends. A service contract may still cover the car after a payoff, but it ends when you no longer have the car after a repossession or total loss. Some states do not require these refunds. The CFPB findings describe what examiners found at certain servicers. They are not a regulation, so your contract and state law still control the amount.

items.title: Credit card late fee larger than your minimum payment, or charged when you paid on time
items.summary: A credit card late fee cannot be more than the minimum payment that was due right before the fee was charged. An issuer cannot set a payment cut-off time earlier than 5 p.m. on the due date. It also cannot charge more than one penalty fee for a single event. The CFPB says its 2024 rule that set an $8 late fee safe harbor for large card issuers was vacated by court order on April 15, 2025.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You have a credit card account that is not secured by your home, and you were charged a late fee or returned-payment fee that is more than your minimum payment, or a late fee on a payment that counts as on time under the rules.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.52(b)(2)(i)(A) and comment 52(b)(2)(i)-1: a late fee cannot exceed the required minimum periodic payment due just before the fee. 12 CFR 1026.52(b)(2)(ii): no more than one penalty fee for a single event or transaction. 12 CFR 1026.52(b)(2)(i)(B): no penalty fee for a declined transaction, account inactivity, or closing the account. 12 CFR 1026.10(b)(2)(ii): cut-off times no earlier than 5 p.m. on the due date. 12 CFR 1026.10(d)(1): if the issuer does not receive or accept mailed payments on the due date, a mailed payment received the next business day is generally not late.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Compare the late fee on your statement with the minimum payment that was due. If the fee is larger, ask for the difference back. 2. Check when your payment arrived. A payment received by 5 p.m. on the due date, a mailed payment received on the next business day when the issuer does not accept mail on the due date, or an in-person payment at the issuer's branch before closing counts as on time. 3. Check whether you were charged both a late fee and a returned-payment fee for the same payment. 4. Call or write the issuer and cite the rule. 5. If it refuses, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: On [date] you charged a late fee of [amount] on account [account number]. The minimum payment due was [amount], and 12 CFR 1026.52(b)(2)(i) does not allow a late fee larger than the minimum payment due. Please refund the difference.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: The same cap applies to returned-payment fees. If you pay electronically or by phone on the next business day, the issuer does not have to treat that payment as on time, even if it does not accept mail on the due date. The $8 late fee limit from the 2024 CFPB rule does not apply because that rule was vacated. Many issuers will also waive a late fee as a courtesy if you ask, but no federal rule requires that.

actions.label: CFPB: Regulation Z, penalty fee limits

items.title: Over-the-limit fee on a credit card you never opted into
items.summary: A credit card issuer cannot charge an over-the-limit fee unless you opted in to let it approve transactions that take you over your credit limit. Even with an opt-in, it can charge only one over-the-limit fee per billing cycle, only if you went over the limit that cycle, and the fee cannot be more than the amount you went over.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You have a credit card account that is not secured by your home, and you were charged an over-the-limit fee without opting in, or you were charged more than the rule allows after opting in.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.56(b)(1): no over-the-limit fee unless the issuer gave you a notice, got your opt-in, and confirmed it. Without your opt-in, the issuer may still approve the transaction but may not charge a fee for it (12 CFR 1026.56(b)(2)). 12 CFR 1026.56(j)(1): no more than one fee per billing cycle, and generally no fee for more than three billing cycles for the same over-the-limit transaction. Comment 52(b)(2)(i)-3: the fee cannot exceed the credit extended over the limit during that billing cycle.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Find the over-the-limit fee on your statement. 2. Contact the issuer. Say you never opted in and ask it to refund the fee. If it says you did, ask for the confirmation it had to send you. 3. If you opted in and want out, revoke it. The issuer must accept revocation by the same methods it allowed for opting in and act on it as soon as reasonably practicable. 4. If it refuses, submit a complaint to the CFPB.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: On [date] you charged me an over-the-limit fee of [amount] on account [account number]. I never opted in to over-the-limit transactions, so under 12 CFR 1026.56 this fee is not allowed. Please refund [amount] and any interest charged on it.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: If you opted in, the issuer can charge the fee, within the limits above. The three-cycle limit does not apply if you make a new over-the-limit transaction in either of the last two billing cycles. On joint accounts, an opt-in or revocation by any one account holder counts for the whole account. A revocation does not apply to transactions made before you told the issuer.

items.title: IRS first-time relief from late filing, late payment and deposit penalties
items.summary: The IRS removes failure-to-file, failure-to-pay and failure-to-deposit penalties of any amount if you timely filed the same return type for the prior three years (or 12 consecutive quarters) with no penalties, apart from the estimated tax penalty. Starting summer 2026, for 2025 tax year returns and 2026 quarterly returns and later, this relief is applied automatically as the Automatic Exemption from Penalty. For earlier years, you ask for First Time Abate by calling the number on your notice or by sending a written statement or Form 843.

fields.label: Who qualifies
fields.value: You timely filed the same type of return for the prior three years (or 12 consecutive quarters), and either no penalty other than the estimated tax penalty was assessed, or a penalty was assessed and later removed for reasonable cause or IRS error. Businesses also must not have had the failure-to-deposit penalty waived four or more times in the prior three years, and the penalty must not be for avoiding EFTPS.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: IRS administrative relief: First Time Abate (FTA) and, from summer 2026, the Automatic Exemption from Penalty (AEP). Covered penalties: failure to file (IRC 6651(a)(1), 6698(a)(1), 6699(a)(1)), failure to pay (IRC 6651(a)(2) and 6651(a)(3)) and failure to deposit (IRC 6656). AEP covers Forms 1040, 1065, 1120, 940, 941, 943, 944, 945 and CT-1.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: For returns before tax year 2025, and for 2025 tax year and 2026 quarterly returns not considered for AEP: 1. Call the IRS at the phone number on your notice or letter, or 2. send a written statement or Form 843, Claim for Refund and Request for Abatement, to the address in the Form 843 instructions. You do not have to name FTA or send supporting documents. Under AEP no action is needed, and you get a letter saying the penalties were not assessed. If you get a notice with a penalty but believe you should have received AEP, contact the IRS. If you do not qualify, you can ask for relief based on reasonable cause.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I am calling about the [penalty type] penalty of [amount] on my notice dated [date] for tax year [year]. I filed on time and had no penalties for the three prior years, so I am asking for first-time penalty relief. Please also remove the interest charged on this penalty.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: When a penalty is reduced or removed, the IRS automatically reduces or removes the interest on it. Under FTA, the failure-to-pay penalty can keep growing until the tax is paid in full. Under AEP, it does not accrue on unpaid tax. You still owe the unpaid tax, interest and any other penalties. FTA and AEP do not apply to returns filed once or infrequently (event-based filing), the Daily Delinquency Penalty, or information reporting that depends on another filing.

items.title: Costco: membership fee refund
items.summary: Costco says it will cancel your membership and refund your membership fee at any time if you are not satisfied. If your US membership auto-renewed on the first of the month, you can ask online for the full renewal amount plus tax back to the card that was charged.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Costco's Risk-Free 100% Satisfaction Guarantee covers the membership itself: Costco will cancel and refund your membership fee at any time if you are dissatisfied. Costco notes that limitations apply. For an auto-renewal charge, the online form refunds the full renewal amount plus applicable taxes to the credit card charged. The form does not do partial refunds.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: The Primary Member must ask. Option 1: go to the membership counter at any Costco warehouse and ask to cancel; Costco says you get the refund right away. Option 2: call Member Services at 1-800-774-2678 and ask a live agent to cancel and refund. Option 3: if your US membership auto-renewed on the first of the month, fill out the Auto Renewal Refund Request form at customerservice.costco.com/app/auto_renewal with the cardholder name, email, membership number and the full renewal amount charged.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I am the Primary Member, and I want to cancel my membership under Costco's 100% Satisfaction Guarantee. Please refund the [amount] membership fee charged on [date].

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: A refund of an auto-renewal charge makes your membership expire at the end of that month unless you renew it. Executive Members: to get the current Executive upgrade fee back, you must cancel or downgrade to Gold Star or Business, and any 2% Reward issued or accrued is subtracted from the refund. Costco says the Reward is not guaranteed to equal the upgrade fee.

actions.label: Costco: how to cancel a membership

items.title: Best Buy: My Best Buy Plus or Total membership refund
items.summary: If you cancel a yearly My Best Buy Plus or Total membership within 60 days of buying or renewing it, you get a full refund for that term, minus the value of benefits you already used. After 60 days, you get a prorated refund for the days left in the billing year, also minus benefits used. For a monthly Total membership, the full-refund window is 20 days after the first purchase and 3 days after each monthly renewal.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Within the window: full refund for the current term. After the window: prorated refund for the days left. In both cases Best Buy may deduct the value of membership benefits, such as product discounts or services, and the price of limited-supply items you bought during priority access or members-only events. Total only: you get back the part of the fee set aside for protection plans, minus any Best Buy Protection repair or replacement costs during the term.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Cancel in one of three ways: call 1-888-BEST-BUY (1-888-237-8289), go to any Best Buy store, or cancel from your online profile at bestbuy.com/services/planlist. If you bought the membership at a Magnolia Design Center inside a Best Buy store, you may need to go to a Magnolia Design Center location for the refund.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I am cancelling my My Best Buy membership, which I bought or renewed on [date], within the refund window in the membership terms. Please refund the [amount] I paid for this term, minus only the benefit value the terms allow.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Cancelling Total also cancels, right away, any Best Buy Protection or AppleCare+ plans that came with it. Best Buy may, at its discretion, let you take over payment to keep a plan. Terms checked: Plus version June 2026, Total version October 2026.

actions.label: Best Buy: My Best Buy Plus terms (PDF)

items.title: Instacart+: annual membership fee refund
items.summary: If you have an annual Instacart+ membership and cancel within the first 5 calendar days of a paid term or renewal, you may get the membership fee back, but only if you have not used Instacart+ benefits in that period. Annual memberships cancelled after 5 days, and all monthly memberships, are not refundable.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Annual plan: cancel within the first 5 calendar days of a paid term or renewal and do not use Instacart+ benefits in that time, and you may get the membership fee back. The help center says this means you have not placed any orders using your Instacart+ membership. After 5 days, annual fees are non-refundable unless the law where you live requires a refund. Monthly plan: fees are not refundable.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Open the menu (three lines at the top left on the website, or the Account icon at the top right in the app). 2. Select Your Instacart+ membership. 3. Under Manage your membership, select Cancel membership. 4. Select Continue to cancel, then Confirm cancellation. 5. Look for the confirmation email, and check your spam folder if you don't see it.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I cancelled my annual Instacart+ membership within 5 calendar days of the [date] charge and have not used any Instacart+ benefits since. Please refund the [amount] membership fee under the Instacart+ terms.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Placing an order with Instacart+ benefits during the 5 days ends the refund option. If you cancel at any other time, there is no refund, but $0 delivery fees continue through the end of the billing period. Some third-party purchases or subscriptions made through Instacart+ may not be refundable.

items.title: Microsoft: subscription refund within 30 days
items.summary: For a subscription bought directly from Microsoft, you may get a refund if you cancel within 30 days of the first purchase or before the first recurring billing date, whichever comes first. You are also entitled to a refund of your most recent recurring charge if you cancel within 30 days after that payment, once per Microsoft account per subscription product.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: First purchase: cancel within 30 days, or before the first recurring billing date if that comes sooner. Renewal: cancel within 30 days after the payment to get the most recent recurring charge back, limited to one time per Microsoft account per subscription product. The United States is not on Microsoft's list of countries with special rules, so the 'All other countries/regions' rows apply: no prorated refunds for Microsoft 365 Basic, Personal, Family, OneDrive and Clipchamp, and for Microsoft 365 Premium and Pro a prorated refund only if you cancel within 14 days of initial purchase.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Sign in to account.microsoft.com/services with the Microsoft account that made the purchase. 2. Go to Services & subscriptions and select the subscription. 3. Choose Manage, then Cancel. 4. During cancellation, Microsoft shows whether the subscription qualifies for a refund and walks you through the next steps.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My Microsoft subscription renewed on [date] and I was charged [amount], which is less than 30 days ago. I am cancelling and ask for a refund of that most recent recurring charge under the Microsoft subscription refund policy.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Not every cancellation results in a refund; eligibility is decided automatically when you cancel. If no refund is issued, Microsoft 365 access usually continues to the end of the billing period. The policy does not cover prepaid retail subscription codes, which follow the store's return policy. If you bought through an app store, ask that store instead. Xbox subscriptions have a separate refund page.

items.title: Ticketmaster: refund for a canceled event
items.summary: If an event is canceled, you don't need to do anything to get a refund. Ticketmaster sends it to your original payment method once it receives the funds from the event organizer, and it should appear within 14 to 21 days. If an event is rescheduled or moved, your tickets stay valid, and you get a refund only if the organizer offers one.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: Canceled event: the refund is automatic and goes to the payment method you used, as soon as Ticketmaster gets the organizer's funds. It should appear within 14 to 21 days, depending on your bank. MLB games, the Masters and the US Open Tennis Championships are exceptions to that timing. Rescheduled or moved event: your tickets, including upgrades and add-ons such as parking, stay valid for the new date. The organizer may offer a refund option; if you take it, the refund should appear within 5 to 7 business days. Ticketmaster can refund only while the organizer authorizes it and the refund window is open.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: Canceled: watch for the refund on the card you paid with, and read the email Ticketmaster sends about your options. Rescheduled or moved: 1. Sign in to your Ticketmaster account. 2. Find the order under My Tickets. 3. If the organizer is offering refunds, a Request Refund button appears; use it before the refund window closes. 4. Ticketmaster emails you a confirmation. Box office purchase for a canceled event: choose your refund options in person 30 days after the organizer approves funds. Box office purchase for a rescheduled event: contact that box office.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: My order for an event that was canceled was charged [amount] on [date], and the refund has not reached my original payment method. Please confirm when the refund will post and the amount being refunded, including any fees I paid.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: Organizers set refund rules event by event, and Ticketmaster can't override a no-refund policy. Different rules apply to transferred and resold tickets. Refunds for lineup or act changes depend on the organizer. The current help pages do not say whether service fees come back with the ticket price, so compare the refund with what you paid and ask if fees are missing.

items.title: American Express: annual fee refund when you close the card
items.summary: American Express refunds the annual fee if you tell it you are voluntarily closing your account within 30 days after the Closing Date of the billing statement that shows the fee. After that 30-day window, the annual fee is not refundable.

fields.label: The rule
fields.value: If you close the account within 30 days after the Closing Date of the statement on which the annual fee appears, Amex refunds that fee. Close later and the fee is non-refundable. This wording is in Amex's US Card Member Agreements as of 03/31/2026, including the Gold Card and the Platinum Card. The policy does not apply if your billing address is in Massachusetts when you close the account.

fields.label: How to get it back
fields.value: 1. Find the billing statement that shows the annual fee and note its Closing Date. 2. Within 30 days after that date, call Amex at the number on the back of your card, or write to Amex, and say you are closing the account. 3. Ask for the annual fee refund under the 30-day rule in your Card Member Agreement. 4. Check your next statement for the credit.

fields.label: What to say
fields.value: I am voluntarily closing my account, and the annual fee of [amount] appeared on the statement that closed on [date], less than 30 days ago. Under my Card Member Agreement, please refund that annual fee.

fields.label: Good to know
fields.value: You still have to pay all charges on the account. If Amex reopens a cancelled account at your request, it may charge a $25 fee. For an Additional Card with its own annual fee, the same refund policy applies when you cancel the card the fee was charged on. The agreement covers closing the account; it says nothing about downgrades. Terms vary by card, so check your own agreement.
